## Summary
This report looks for a core microbial community in acid mine drainage (AMD) water across 103 publicly archived metagenomes from six BioProjects. The approach is k-mer-based and doesn’t depend on location; it was first developed for pig gut microbiome work. Each metagenome is searched against the GTDB rs226 species-level pangenome sketch using sourmash branchwater manysearch, with no minimum threshold, so low-abundance taxa are kept and filtering happens afterward. Species prevalence is summarized across samples, and core candidates are species present in at least 95% of metagenomes. These results are shown at several containment thresholds (0.05, 0.10 and 0.20) so you can see how sensitive the core is to the cutoff. Candidates are compared with the five core genera from prior metagenome-based work by M. Tran (126 metagenomes from the same BioProjects) and with well-known AMD acidophiles such as Acidithiobacillus, Leptospirillum, Ferrovum and Gallionella.
